titleEn: Why can't we remember our earliest years?
summaryEn:
You may remember your first day at school, but you almost certainly do not remember your first birthday or the first time you learned to walk.

Most adults have very few autobiographical memories from before about age 3, and memories of the following years are also much sparser than those from adulthood.

This phenomenon is called infantile amnesia.

The strange thing is that young children still learn and remember very well. So where did those earliest memories go?
